rationale: The glossary entry's central claim redefines ḥodesh ('renewed/new moon') as the full-moon phase that begins the month (with east-gate and moedim-sign elaborations). The supplied texts and chapter arguments do not carry this identification better than the ordinary calendrical reading. Psalm 81:3's juxtaposition of ḥodesh and keseh is most naturally read as poetic pairing or sequential feast markers, not definitional equation; Job 10:17's 'renewest thy witnesses' is an independent lament construction that does not lexicalize lunar phase; Psalm 89:36-37 establishes the moon as enduring witness without fixing its phase as month-start; Ezekiel 46 opens the east gate on new-moon day without equating that day to full-moon rise; 1 Samuel 20 assumes advance knowledge of the day without requiring full-moon predictability; Isaiah 66:23, Amos 8:5 and Colossians 2:16-17 treat new moons as recurring cultic occasions (or shadows) without phase redefinition. The cumulative case therefore rests on contested etymology, pictographic speculation, selective parallelism, and calendar-wide inferences that the texts themselves do not compel. The ordinary reading accounts for the same verses with fewer unsupported steps.
book_core_identification: The renewed moon (biblical new moon/ḥodesh) is the full-moon phase that marks the start of the month.
book_secondary_elaborations: the full moon appears in the east gate
the full moon is the sign of the appointed times
unsupported_glossary_assertions: The renewed moon is the full-moon phase
The full moon marks the start of the month
The full moon stands in the east gate as the defining new-moon marker
The full moon is the sign of the appointed times
chapter_only_objections: Pearl-as-full-moon/bride typology and merchant purchase allegory
Proverbs 31 woman as lunar portrait and sapphire/throne wordplay
Full-moon calendar reconstruction (Abib start, feast dating, crucifixion darkness alignment, Sirach support, Mazzaroth/tribe gates)
Pictographic letter theology and 'no shadow of turning' applied to lunar phases
Claims that traditional dark/crescent calendars are solely Egyptian or 'traditions of men' nullifying Torah
strongest_counter_interpretation: Biblical 'new moon' (ḥodesh) denotes the ordinary start of the lunar month at conjunction or first crescent visibility—the recognized cultic day of offerings, trumpet, and cessation—functioning within Israel's appointed-times calendar and later identified in Colossians 2:16-17 as a ceremonial shadow fulfilled in Christ; full moon (keseh) is a distinct mid-month phase or feast marker, not the definition of ḥodesh.
counter_core_identification: New moon is the dark-moon or crescent phase that begins the month as a ceremonial appointed time.
material_core_denial: The new moon is not the full moon, and the full moon does not mark the start of the biblical month.
counter_case: Numbers 10:10; 28:11-15 and 1 Samuel 20 treat new moon as a known monthly feast day without any full-moon equation
Psalm 81:3 is standardly read as new-moon trumpet plus full-moon/feast (or 'appointed time') rather than identity; the KJV and many witnesses do not force synonymy
Ezekiel 46:1-3 simply opens the east gate on new-moon day for worship; it does not identify the moon's phase or require full-moon rise as the definition of the day
Isaiah 66:23 and Amos 8:5 use new moon as a recurring calendrical marker of worship or commerce pause, consistent with ordinary lunar-month start
Colossians 2:16-17 places new moons among shadows whose substance is Christ, matching the mainstream ceremonial reading and offering no phase redefinition
Ancient Near Eastern and Second-Temple practice uniformly began months at dark or crescent; the texts nowhere overturn that usage with an explicit full-moon start rule
book_explanatory_advantages: Attempts to give ḥodesh a concrete visual content (complete illuminated disk) via root 'renew to perfection'
Links Psalm 89 witness language and Job 10:17 'renewed witnesses' to opposition geometry of full moon
Notes east-gate opening and full-moon rise direction as a possible geometric fit
counter_explanatory_advantages: Preserves the plain, widely attested sense of ḥodesh as month-beginning without retranslating or equating distinct terms
Accounts for all listed verses as ordinary cultic calendar references plus typological shadow without requiring pictographs, throne-letter identity, or global calendar inversion
Fits the observational and narrative data of 1 Samuel 20 under either calculated or averaged lunar cycles known in antiquity
Requires no special pleading against the uniform ancient practice presupposed by the biblical writers themselves
evidence_book_core_cannot_explain: The absence of any explicit scriptural statement that the month begins at full moon or that ḥodesh means full moon
Colossians 2:16-17's classification of new moons as shadows whose body is Christ, which functions equally well (and more simply) under the ordinary calendrical sense
The routine narrative expectation in 1 Samuel 20 and the sacrificial prescriptions that treat new moon as a fixed monthly institution without full-moon markers
Isaiah 1:13-14 and Hosea 2:11's critique of new moons as empty ritual, which presupposes the established ceremonial day rather than a redefined full-moon start
decisive_sources: Numbers 28:11-15 (implied by entry context and common basis)
unresolved_objections: Whether keseh in Psalm 81:3 can ever be pressed into strict identity with ḥodesh rather than parallel or sequential feast language
Degree to which east-gate geometry and full-moon opposition can be elevated from possible illustration to definitional proof
